_meta.indication: BENLYSTA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with active, autoantibody-positive, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) who are receiving standard therapy.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study C1056 (BLISS; HGS1006/LymphoStat-B), a Phase 3 76-week study in SLE
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized to placebo or belimumab 1 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg by IV infusion
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy; conducted primarily in US, Canada, and Western Europe (78% of patients)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SLE Responder Index (SRI) response at week 52
pivotal_trials.result: SRI response at week 52: 43% belimumab 10 mg/kg vs 34% placebo (OR 1.52, 95% CI 1.07, 2.15; p=0.0207)

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study C1057 (BLISS; HGS1006/LymphoStat-B), a Phase 3 52-week study in SLE
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study; patients randomized to placebo or belimumab 1 mg/kg or 10 mg/kg by IV infusion
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with active, autoantibody-positive SLE on standard therapy; conducted primarily in Latin America and Asia (88% of patients)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: SLE Responder Index (SRI) response at week 52
pivotal_trials.result: SRI response at week 52: 58% belimumab 10 mg/kg vs 44% placebo (OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.3, 2.59; p=0.0006)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were nausea (15% vs 12% placebo), diarrhea (12% vs 9%), pyrexia, nasopharyngitis, bronchitis (9% vs 5%), insomnia, pain in extremity, depression, migraine, and pharyngitis. Serious concerns included more deaths with BENLYSTA than placebo (14 deaths out of 2133 patients), serious and sometimes fatal infections, and infusion/hypersensitivity reactions (infusion-associated AEs in 17% BENLYSTA vs 15% placebo).
target_moa: Belimumab is a human IgG1λ monoclonal antibody that binds soluble human B-lymphocyte stimulator (BLyS/BAFF) and inhibits its biological activity, a BLyS-specific inhibitor.

rems.type: FDA determined that at this time a REMS is not necessary for Benlysta (belimumab) to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.

advisory_committee.vote: Arthritis Advisory Committee (November 16, 2010): substantial evidence of efficacy 10 yes / 5 no; safety profile 14 yes / 1 no; approvability 13 yes / 2 no.

summary.text: Benlysta (belimumab) was submitted June 9, 2010 and reviewed as a Priority BLA, supported by Phase 3 studies C1056 and C1057 demonstrating higher SRI response at week 52 with 10 mg/kg vs placebo; an Arthritis Advisory Committee voted in favor of approval (13 yes, 2 no), and FDA approved it March 9, 2011 as a full (traditional) approval with no REMS required.

Regarding the approvability question, which is essentially the sum of demonstration of efficacy and safety, the results were in favor of approval (13 yes, 2 no).
We have determined that at this time, a REMS is not necessary for Benlysta (belimumab) to ensure that its benefits outweigh its risks.
